title: Runtime Canary Telemetry Envelope and Fast Fallback Lattice — Design & Playbook
author: Maya Singh
content:
Overview:

This document defines a lightweight, runtime-friendly telemetry envelope to be emitted by API gateways and runtime proxies for canary cohorts, plus a deterministic "fast fallback lattice" that uses those signals to make low-latency routing and rollback decisions. It combines an API contract (the envelope), a metric gating matrix (canary pass/fail thresholds), and an operational playbook for automation and manual intervention.

Goals:
- Provide a single, compact telemetry envelope that is sufficient for automated canary gating and for post-hoc forensic analysis without high cardinality explosion.
- Define deterministic fallback decision logic that can be executed at the edge or control plane within 50ms of telemetry arrival.
- Specify SLOs and alerting thresholds for canary health and fallback stability.
- Provide an operational runbook for safe canary rollout, automatic fallback, and manual rollback.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to: public API endpoints, streaming endpoints, and model-serving gRPC frontends.
- Not in scope: deep batch jobs, offline evaluation harnesses.
- Intended consumers: gateway proxy, control-plane canary service, alerting pipeline, and engineering oncall.

Design summary (short):
1) Telemetry envelope: a JSON object with a small set of canonical fields (ids, timestamps, compact metrics, tags). Producers: edge proxies and runtime sidecars.
2) Canary gating: compute small set of aggregations per canary window (1m, 5m) and compare to thresholds.
3) Fast fallback lattice: prioritized decision graph of fallback actions (local replica switch, model-variant switch, global fallback + degraded response). Each action has required conditions and cooldowns.

Telemetry envelope specification (contract):
- Envelope name: redwood.runtime.canary.v1
- Emission semantics: emitted per request at completion, or at periodic window flush for streaming sessions. Envelope must be small (<1KB).
- Fields (compact table):

| field_name           | type   | required | description |
|----------------------|--------|----------|-------------|
| envelope_id          | string | yes      | UUID per emitted envelope |
| service              | string | yes      | logical service name (e.g., inference.edge-api) |
| route                | string | yes      | API route or model id |
| cohort               | string | conditional | canary cohort id (empty for production) |
| tenant_id            | string | conditional | tenant scope if multi-tenant |
| outcome              | string | yes      | success|user_error|server_error|timeout |
| latency_ms           | int    | yes      | end-to-end latency in ms |
| tokens_consumed      | int    | optional | token count for generation calls |
| sample_rate          | float  | yes      | fraction [0.0-1.0] that this envelope represents when sampling is applied |
| timestamp            | string | yes      | RFC3339 UTC timestamp |
| model_variant        | string | optional | model/quantization tag |
| trace_id             | string | optional | trace id for correlation |
| extra_tags           | string | optional | comma-separated short tags (region=us-east1, tier=premium) |

Note: To keep ingestion cost down, producers should respect cluster-configured sampling. sample_rate must be set so aggregation can weight counts back to actuals.

Example envelope (single-line):
{"envelope_id":"b3f2d8a4-72a1-4b7e-9d6c-1f7f9c4d5e6a","service":"inference.edge-api","route":"/v1/generate","cohort":"canary-2026-02-20-a","outcome":"success","latency_ms":162,"tokens_consumed":34,"sample_rate":0.1,"timestamp":"2026-02-20T15:42:03Z","model_variant":"redwood-3b-q8"}

Aggregation and gating matrix:
- Aggregations to compute per-cohort, per-route, per-window (windows: 1m, 5m): total_requests, weighted_errors, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, avg_tokens.
- Weighted counts: for sampled envelopes, weight = 1 / sample_rate.

Gating thresholds (recommended defaults):
| metric           | window | canary pass condition (default) |
|------------------|--------|----------------------------------|
| weighted_errors  | 1m,5m  | error_rate < 0.5% (errors/requests) |
| p95_latency_ms   | 1m,5m  | p95 < 200ms for interactive routes, <400ms for batch-like routes |
| p50_latency_ms   | 1m     | p50 < 100ms (interactive) |
| token_usage_rate | 5m     | avg_tokens within +-20% of baseline |
| synthetic-failure-rate | 1m | synthetic check failures < 0.1% |
All thresholds are tunable per product. Canary is considered failed if ANY two metrics in the 1m window violate their thresholds, or a single severe violation occurs (server_error spikes >1% across 1m).

Fast fallback lattice (concept):
- The lattice is an ordered set of actions with conditions and cooldowns. Each node returns one of: NO_OP, ROUTE_SHIFT, VARIANT_SWAP, GLOBAL_DEGRADE, FORCE_ROLLBACK.
- Order (highest priority first):
  1) FORCE_ROLLBACK: triggered when escalation criteria met (see runbook). Immediate full rollback to previous production variant. Cooldown: 15m.
  2) VARIANT_SWAP: switch to compatible model variant (e.g., float32 -> q4f16) on the same shard to maintain service continuity. Cooldown: 5m.
  3) ROUTE_SHIFT: route affected requests to warm standby pool in a different AZ/region. Cooldown: 3m.
  4) GLOBAL_DEGRADE: enable degraded response mode (shorter max tokens, limited tool calls) for affected routes. Cooldown: 2m.
  5) NO_OP: if none of the above conditions meet.

Decision input and evaluation latency:
- Decision inputs: 1m and 5m aggregations from the telemetry ingestion service, plus active capacity signals from scheduler (node_pressure metric), and explicit operator overrides from the control plane.
- Evaluation target: <50ms from ingestion to decision outcome for a single routed event (edge-exec mode).

Pseudocode (simplified):
if escalation_criteria(enrich(aggregates, capacity_signals)):
  action = FORCE_ROLLBACK
else if variant_swap_condition(aggregates):
  action = VARIANT_SWAP
else if route_shift_condition(aggregates, node_pressure):
  action = ROUTE_SHIFT
else if degrade_condition(aggregates):
  action = GLOBAL_DEGRADE
else:
  action = NO_OP

Escalation criteria (examples):
- weighted_errors (1m) > 2% AND p95_latency_ms > 2x baseline OR
- server_error spike > 1% sustained for 2 consecutive 1m windows OR
- synthetic-failure-rate > 0.5% AND capacity shortfall > 30%

Runbook: Canary rollout and automated fallback steps:
1) Pre-checks (owner: release-engineering):
   - Confirm baseline metrics for the route (p50/p95/err) for last 24h are recorded in the canary dashboard.
   - Configure cohort id and sampling for telemetry (sample_rate recommended 0.1 for canary).
   - Schedule canary window and alert thresholds.
2) Canary start (automated):
   - Deploy variant to 1% cohort routed via traffic-split rule.
   - Begin telemetry collection; verify envelope emission and ingestion (sanity check: >100 weighted requests in first 5m).
3) Automatic gating (control-plane):
   - Evaluate 1m windows. If gating failure detected, execute lattice evaluation and perform the top-ranked permitted action. Log action in audit stream.
4) Operator notification (oncall):
   - If FORCE_ROLLBACK chosen, page oncall with severity P0. Page must include cohort id, offending metrics, last 10 envelopes sample and trace links.
5) Post-action stability window:
   - After any automatic action, enter 15m safety window where automated second-order escalations are inhibited to avoid flip-flopping.
6) Manual rollback:
   - If automated actions did not restore service, runbook commander will perform manual rollback using release orchestration tooling and notify customers as per escalation policy.

Alerting and SLOs (recommended):
- Canary health alert: fire when any two gating thresholds are violated within 1m at cohort > 0.5% traffic. Severity P1.
- Forced rollback alert: fire on FORCE_ROLLBACK action. Severity P0.
- SLOs for production routes (examples): p95_latency_ms < 200ms, overall_error_rate < 0.2%, availability 99.95%.

Telemetry cost and sampling guidance:
- Default canary sampling: 10% (0.1) during first 30m; reduce to 1% if stable and long retention is a cost concern.
- For multi-tenant routes, always sample all tenant_ids that are part of contract tests; otherwise use probabilistic sampling stratified by tenant_id.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Service owner: teams that own the route must ensure emission of the envelope and have a current canary dashboard.
- Control-plane: runtime-canary-service responsible for aggregation, lattice evaluation, and executing permitted actions.
- Observability: responsible for alerting rules and SLO dashboards.

Implementation notes and compatibility:
- Envelope versioning: producers must set redwood.runtime.canary.vX in header; control-plane will accept v1 and v2 with backward compatibility shim for deprecated fields.
- Backfill behavior: when sample_rate is <1.0, aggregators must scale counts using 1/sample_rate.
- Security: no PII in extra_tags; tenant_id must be hashed if tenant privacy is required.

Testing and validation checklist (pre-deploy):
1) Unit tests for envelope serializer and sampling weight computation.
2) Integration test: synthetic canary that injects 1% traffic and fails synthetic checks to validate FORCE_ROLLBACK path.
3) Chaos test: simulate node_pressure to validate ROUTE_SHIFT path.
4) Observability test: validate that trace ids and sample logs are linked to canary_id and surfaced in runbook links.

Appendix: sample alert message (template):
Subject: [P0] Canary FORCE_ROLLBACK — route=/v1/generate cohort=canary-2026-02-20-a
Body:
- Trigger: weighted_errors 1m = 2.7% (threshold 0.5%), p95=480ms (threshold 200ms)
- Action: FORCE_ROLLBACK executed at 2026-02-20T15:49:34Z by runtime-canary-service v1.12
- Links: canary dashboard | trace samples | release runbook | audit log id: a3f7d

Concluding notes:
This playbook is intentionally conservative: it prefers simple, deterministic actions that can be reasoned about quickly during oncall. Teams should adapt thresholds to product needs but must preserve the ordered lattice semantics and cooldowns to avoid oscillation.
